title: Hammock localization presents universal infinity localization
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category and let $W$ be a wide subcategory, containing every identity. Enlarge universes so that $\mathcal C$ and all the diagram categories below are small. The hammock localization $L^H(\mathcal C,W)$ is a category enriched in simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with the same objects as $\mathcal C$. Its mapping simplicial set from $x$ to $y$ has as $k$-simplices reduced commutative hammocks of width $k$: $k+1$ rows of finite zigzags from $x$ to $y$, all vertical maps pointing down and belonging to $W$, identity vertical maps at the endpoints, all horizontal maps in any column pointing in the same direction, leftward horizontal maps in $W$, adjacent columns pointing in opposite directions, and no column consisting entirely of identities. Faces and degeneracies delete or repeat rows and then reduce by composing adjacent like-directed columns and deleting identity columns. Composition concatenates and reduces hammocks. Choose a fibrant replacement of this enriched category that induces weak homotopy equivalences on mapping simplicial sets, so its mapping objects are Kan complexes. The homotopy coherent nerve of this replacement is an infinity category $\mathcal L$ and the induced $q:N\mathcal C\to\mathcal L$ is a universal infinity localization at $W$: for every infinity category $\mathcal E$, precomposition identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)$ with the full infinity subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ on functors sending $W$ to equivalences. Here the ordinary nerve has composable strings as simplices; the homotopy coherent nerve has in degree $n$ enriched functors from the simplicial coherent realization of $\Delta^n$; and an infinity category is a simplicial set filling every inner horn. In particular $L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)$ represents $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(qx,qy)$, its length-one hammocks represent $q$ on actual maps, and these comparisons are natural for functors preserving $W$, respecting composition and its homotopies.

source.place: Barnea–Harpaz–Horel, Pro-categories in homotopy theory, Section 2.2, Definition 2.2.1 and the following universal property and construction (1), printed pp. 579–580; Remark 2.2.2 for replacement fixing objects. This covers an arbitrary wide subcategory, without a saturation assumption. Hammock formulas are Low Definition 3.1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dk-cofibrant-localization-comparison] to $(\mathcal C,W)$. Its $H(\mathcal C,W)$ is exactly the reduced-hammock construction in the statement, including the length-zero identity and row-deletion/repetition followed by reduction. Thus the operations in the question define the claimed simplicial category and its actual-map functor. In particular deleting an identity column never deletes the identity morphism of the enriched category: the surviving identity is the hammock of length zero.

Set $A=F_\bullet W$, $B=F_\bullet\mathcal C$, and $V=B[A^{-1}]$. By [lem-coef-dk-cofibrant-localization-comparison], $A\to B$ is a cofibration of cofibrant simplicial categories on $O=\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C$, and its augmentation is a mapping-set equivalence to $W\to\mathcal C$. The same node supplies the enriched span $L^H(\mathcal C,W)\leftarrow H_F\to V$ of mapping-set weak equivalences. By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], applying the derived coherent nerve turns this span into equivalences of infinity categories. The span is compatible with the augmented maps from $B$; hence its equivalence identifies the functor $N\mathcal C\to\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}V$ with the one induced by actual-map hammocks. This records the localization map, not just an equivalence between unpointed objects.

source.place: Proposition 2.2 and its augmentation-compatible comparison span, printed pp.19-20

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cofibrant-simplicial-inversion] to this specific cofibrant inclusion $A\to B$. It gives a homotopy pushout $V\simeq B\amalg_A^hG(A)$, where $G(A)$ is degreewise total inversion of $A$. Its total-inversion map has the additional property that $K=\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}A\to S=\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}G(A)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $S$ is Kan. The cofibrancy and fixed-object hypotheses are precisely those verified in step 2. No closure property is being imposed on $W$.

source.place: Sections 8.1-8.2, 9.2 and 10.1; Hinich Section 1.2 before Proposition 1.2.1

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], the homotopy pushout of step 3 becomes a pushout in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The augmentations in [lem-coef-dk-cofibrant-localization-comparison] identify $\mathbf RN_{\mathrm{hc}}B\simeq N\mathcal C$ and $K\simeq NW$, compatibly with their map. Thus if $\mathcal L$ denotes the coherent nerve of an object-preserving locally Kan replacement of $L^H(\mathcal C,W)$, steps 2-3 present it under $N\mathcal C$ as
$$\mathcal L\simeq N\mathcal C\amalg_{K}S,$$
where $K\to N\mathcal C$ is the augmentation to $NW$ followed by the inclusion. The original hammock category maps by mapping-set weak equivalences to both any chosen replacement and the functorial object-preserving replacement; this zigzag is under the actual-map functor from $\mathcal C$. Hence changing to another replacement of the stipulated kind changes this presentation by a zigzag of mapping-set equivalences and hence by an equivalence under $N\mathcal C$.

source.place: Section 1.2, cocartesian diagram (5) and the coherent-nerve Quillen equivalence; Barnea--Harpaz--Horel Section 2.2 construction (1)

proof.text: For any infinity category $\mathcal E$ apply the existing [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] to the actual map $K\to S$ from step 3. Its two hypotheses are exactly that $S$ is Kan and $K\to S$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. It identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal E)$ with the full infinity subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ on the diagrams inverting all edges of $K$, with all their transformations. Use the replacement $R$ that fixes discrete categories, as specified in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. The augmentation gives the actual map $K\to NW$. Every edge of $K$ maps to an arrow of $W$, and every arrow $w$ of $W$ is the image of an edge of $K$: take its free generator in degree zero of $F_\bullet W$, or the identity for an identity arrow, and then apply $A\to RA$. Thus for a diagram $D:NW\to\mathcal E$, its restriction to $K$ inverts all edges if and only if $D$ inverts every arrow of $W$. This verifies the inversion criterion directly for the restriction used in step 6.

source.place: Proposition 6.3.1.21 (01MY), with Definition 6.3.1.9 and Proposition 6.3.1.13 (01MS), the exact source intent recorded by lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization. The concrete augmentation edge criterion is elementary from the free-resolution and replacement statements.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout] to the pushout of step 4. This gives, naturally in $\mathcal E$,
$$\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal L,\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal C,\mathcal E)\mathop{\times}^{h}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal E).$$
The projection to the first factor is precomposition with the actual-map functor $q$ identified in steps 2 and 4. In particular this formula controls coherent transformations and their mapping spaces as well as the objects.

source.place: Cartesian internal-Hom calculus of Sections 3.1.3-3.1.4 and the pushout universal property

proof.text: Using the full-subcategory description in step 5, the pullback in step 6 is the full subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(N\mathcal C,\mathcal E)$ whose objects restrict to the indicated full subcategory over $K$. Explicitly an object $F$ admits an extension datum exactly when its restriction inverts every edge of $K$; the space of that datum is contractible because restriction from $S$ is fully faithful. Between two such $F,F'$, every coherent transformation of the restrictions lifts uniquely up to a contractible space, and its higher compatibilities lift in the same mapping-space fiber. Thus the projection is fully faithful with essential image exactly those $F$ for which $F(w)$ is an equivalence for every $w\in W$. This proves the requested universal property on the entire functor infinity category. The argument never replaces $W$ by an assumed saturated subcategory.

source.place: Section 1.1.2 pushout formula; elementary pullback of the full subcategory specified by the cited groupoid-localization theorem

proof.text:
For $x,y\in\mathcal C$, the replacement map gives a weak homotopy equivalence $L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)\to R L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)$. Apply the mapping-space part of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] to the locally Kan target. It gives
$$L^H(\mathcal C,W)(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal L}(qx,qy).$$
The vertex correspondence in that theorem sends the vertex represented by a one-arrow hammock to its coherent-nerve edge. Together with the actual-map functor of step 1 this is $q(f)$ for every actual map $f:x\to y$; identities use the length-zero case.

Let $T:(\mathcal C,W)\to(\mathcal C',W')$ preserve the distinguished arrows. Apply $T$ to every object and arrow of a hammock and then reduce; this commutes with row operators, and with concatenation and reduction. The natural enriched span of [lem-coef-dk-cofibrant-localization-comparison] and the natural cofibrant-inversion square of [lem-coef-cofibrant-simplicial-inversion] identify the resulting map with the map of the pushouts used above. Naturality of [lem-cbc-simplicial-groupoid-localization] and [lem-coef-infinity-functor-pushout] identifies the restriction comparison with the universal localized functor for $T$. Finally [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] gives natural mapping-space comparisons preserving enriched composition and its coherent homotopies. Since the input is a simplicial functor and the comparison is induced by the enriched nerve adjunction, this compatibility holds on all simplices, including the simplices recording composition homotopies. It is not merely equality after taking $\pi_0$.
